newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs seen weaker on new corruption charges.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs seen weaker on new corruption charges.

text.p: Brazil stocks are seen opening lower after a local newspaper said Communications Minister Sergio Motta was linked to a new corruption scandal in Congress, brokers said.

Folha de Sao Paulo daily said it had obtained new secretly taped conversations of deputies who were allegedly paid to vote for a bill allowing presidential re-election which showed Motta had provided some of the money to buy the votes. "As far as I know it's like this. It was the 200 from Serjao (Sergio Motta), via Amazonino, that were the federal contribution to the accord," the paper quoted Deputy Joao Maia as saying.
"The situation is confusing. In doubt, investors are likely to sell," said a senior trader.
Analysts fear that the new allegations will paralyze Congress and put on hold key constitutional reforms and bills to be voted by lawmakers.
A lower house panel mulling a new telecoms law was due to vote today on the bill, but, with the new corruption charges, the voting could be postponed, traders said.
